Vedanta Ltd Unveils New Sustainable Aluminium Alloy, Eyes Boost in Regional Manufacturing

Vedanta Ltd, a leader in India’s metals and mining sector, has announced the launch of a new sustainable aluminium alloy, aiming to strengthen its foothold in the domestic manufacturing landscape. The product, named GreenLite Alloy, was introduced at a ceremony at the company’s Jharsuguda plant in Odisha on Wednesday, attended by industry officials, local government representatives, and trade association members.

Company executives highlighted the alloy’s lower carbon footprint and its potential to meet the rising demand from automotive, construction, and electrical industries. “GreenLite Alloy marks a significant step in our commitment to sustainability and innovation,” said Arvind Kumar, Vedanta Ltd’s Chief Operating Officer for Aluminium. “This product is engineered to not only reduce environmental impact but also to deliver enhanced performance for our clients.”

The new alloy incorporates recycled aluminium and employs energy-efficient processing techniques, according to the company. Vedanta Ltd claims that the GreenLite Alloy reduces greenhouse gas emissions by up to 30% compared to conventional alternatives. The company expects to produce up to 50,000 tonnes of the new alloy in the first year, with plans to scale up production based on market response.

Industry experts have welcomed the move, noting its alignment with broader trends in both the domestic and global metals market. “With India’s focus on reducing industrial emissions and promoting clean manufacturing, products like GreenLite Alloy can give local manufacturers a competitive edge,” said Priya Saha, a senior analyst at the Indian Metals Federation. “It’s encouraging to see major producers investing in sustainable materials.”

Local officials also praised the initiative for its potential to generate new employment and support ancillary industries. “Vedanta Ltd’s investment in next-generation materials is a boost for regional development,” stated Subhash Mishra, Additional District Magistrate of Jharsuguda. “We anticipate positive ripple effects for small and medium enterprises in the area.”

The launch arrives amid growing demand for sustainable raw materials from both domestic and export markets. Representatives from the Odisha Metalworkers’ Association expressed optimism that the new product could open up further opportunities for skill development and training in the region.

Vedanta Ltd said it would work closely with its downstream partners to integrate GreenLite Alloy into supply chains, and is planning technical workshops to familiarize manufacturers with the new material’s properties and applications.
